incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1735554321 - GPU queue growth + autoscaler saturating. Severity: P1. Affected: hosted inference (us-west2). Paging oncall: Alex (oncall).

Alex (oncall): I just got paged, looking. What's the observed impact?

Priya (sre): Queue length for gpu-pool-usw2 jumped ~6x in last 10m. Autoscaler is at max replicas and not provisioning new spot capacity due to repeated preemptions. Throttling active for lower-tier routes.

Mateo (platform): Confirmed. Metrics: queued_requests ~ 12k (baseline 1.8k), avg_wait ~ 18s (baseline 2s). Autoscaler replicas=78 (max=80). Spot pool preemptions spiked, fallback capacity (reserved/dedicated) not configured for this account of pools so routing couldn't failover.

Alex (oncall): Any immediate customer impact?

Sam (cust-success): Some customers on high-throughput plans are reporting increased latency and token errors. We have two intercom threads open (cust-214, cust-337) — they're seeing timeouts and 429-like behavior.

Lina (eng-runtime): Logs show model workers failing to attach KV cache after preemption and restarting repeatedly. Also seeing error rate from sidecar: `ERR_INSufficientFallback`.

Priya (sre): Action plan attempt 1: throttle back non-critical async batch routes, prioritize production synchronous routes. I'll push a rate-limit policy change for the tenant-level quotas.

Alex (oncall): Go ahead. Priya, call when done. Mateo, can we temporarily increase max replicas?

Mateo (platform): We can raise max_replicas to 120 but cluster spot quotas may prevent actual nodes from appearing. Also we risk more churn if preemptions continue. I can submit the change now but it won't help if cloud can't supply GPUs.

deploy-bot: deploy started by Priya: `sre/throttle-async-batches` -> staging -> canary -> prod

Priya (sre): Throttle change applied. Non-critical batch workers reduced to 30% of prior throughput. Observability notes: queue reduced slightly, but still trending upward.

Alex (oncall): Do we have any fallback model variants (CPU) we can route to temporarily? Even slower but keeps customers alive.

Lina (eng-runtime): We have a smaller-variant (quantized) CPU-compatible model, but routing logic only fails over to that for Dedicated customers currently. For hosted, failover is disabled by default to avoid cost surprises. We can enable policy at route-level for specific tenants.

Mateo (platform): I can flip a conservative failover policy to allow routing to cpu-quant for top 5 impacted tenants. Need approval due to potential cost and degraded latency.

Sam (cust-success): Approve for cust-214 and cust-337, we told them we'd do whatever keeps them online.

Alex (oncall): Priya, once throttle steady, do failover for those two tenants only. Coordinate with Sam so CS informs customers.

Priya (sre): Doing it now. Patching routing policy: `route.failover.cpu_quantized=true` for tenants {214,337}.

Priya (sre): Pushed. Verified that requests for those tenants are hitting cpu-quant variant. Latency is higher but success rate improved for cust-214.

Lina (eng-runtime): Meanwhile I'm seeing kube events showing node drain churn due to spot preemptions. Attaching snippet:

```
NAME                           STATUS   REASON                    AGE
gpunode-spot-4-abcde           NotReady Preempted                3m
gpunode-spot-7-fghij           NotReady Preempted                2m
pods evicted: 24, rescheduled: 18
```

Mateo (platform): Cloud provider reporting a capacity shortage in us-west2 GPU zone. Requesting capacity now but ETA unknown.

Alex (oncall): If cloud ETA > 20m this becomes customer-impacting at scale. What's the plan for longer-term mitigations?

Mateo (platform): Options: 1) Force allocation to on-demand/dedicated nodes (fast but expensive), 2) Redeploy some workloads to another region (latency/regulatory impacts), 3) Enforce stricter throttles and queue backpressure. I'll start option 1 as emergency measure for critical routes. Need approval for cost.

Sam (cust-success): CS recommends option 1 for top paying customers. They want uptime > everything right now.

Alex (oncall): Approve emergency on-demand allocation for top 10 customers for next 2 hours. Mateo, spin up dedicated nodes and ensure isolation (no noisy neighbor).

Mateo (platform): Spinning up 12 on-demand GPU instances in us-west2 now. Will attach to dedicated-pool-temp. Estimated ready in ~6-8 minutes.

deploy-bot: resource-allocation: created dedicated-pool-temp (12 nodes) by Mateo

Priya (sre): Once nodes ready, I'll update routing to prefer dedicated-pool-temp for top10. Also enabling circuit-breaker for non-critical tenants.

Lina (eng-runtime): Note: Some in-flight KV cache warmups will fail during migration. We'll see transient 5xx for few requests. Prepare customer comms.

Alex (oncall): Sam, can CS draft a short note for affected customers: acknowledging latency increases, describing mitigation (routing to CPU variant / dedicated nodes) and expected timeframe (2 hours)?

Sam (cust-success): On it. Drafted message and sending to legal for review. Quick version: "We're experiencing GPU capacity issues in us-west2; we're routing critical requests to reserved capacity and lower-latency fallbacks to reduce errors. Expect improved success within 15 minutes and full stabilization within 2 hours."

Priya (sre): Dedicated nodes are registerING... routing updates applied for top10. Early telemetry: queue for top10 dropped 90%, overall queue down 40%. Good signal.

Mateo (platform): Cloud provider sent notice: additional spot capacity available in 30-45m. We'll keep on-demand pool for now, and scale down once spot stabilizes.

Lina (eng-runtime): Doing a root-cause trace: looks like a combination of provider-side GPU scarcity + our autoscaler not quickly evicting low-priority pods because `podDisruptionBudget` blocked evictions. We should adjust PDB logic to allow emergency preemption for non-critical workloads.

Alex (oncall): Action items:
- Priya: monitor and keep throttles in place, validate no new SLO breaches (ETA 15m).
- Mateo: keep dedicated-pool-temp live, scale if needed, work with cloud contacts for spot capacity ETA.
- Lina: prepare a PDB change proposal to allow emergency eviction for non-critical pods.
- Sam: send customer comms once legal signs off.

Priya (sre): Noted. Monitoring boards updated. Setting recurring 5m updates here.

Alex (oncall): Handing off to Priya for ongoing mitigation. I'll remain reachable for escalation. Priya, take over the thread.

Priya (sre): Acknowledged. Handoff to Priya (sre). :hand:

incident-bot: oncall-handoff: previous_oncall=Alex (oncall) new_oncall=Priya (sre) at 1735556720

Priya (sre): 1735556720 update: queue stabilized further, total queued down to ~3.2k. Dedicated-pool-temp handling 85% of top10. Still watching spot churn. Next update in 5m.

Sam (cust-success): Legal approved. Message sent to affected customers. Early gratitude from cust-214.

Mateo (platform): 1735556880 update: added autoscaler safety-checks to avoid flapping by ignoring preemption spikes for 2m windows. Will follow up with change to PDB logic in PR later today.

Lina (eng-runtime): Logging post-mortem placeholder: `gpu-capacity-exhaustion-1735554321`. I'll capture timeline and recommend: enable per-tenant failover policies by default for paid tiers, and revisit autoscaler max vs guaranteed capacity ratios.

Priya (sre): Closing active mitigation window in 10m if metrics hold. Leaving this channel open for followups and postmortem notes.

incident-bot: Incident 1735554321 status changed to: mitigated (P1 -> P2) at 1735556880
